nodes.label: Desktop app
nodes.summary: The Electron front end of the daemon: the product window and the HUD.

nodes.label: HUD
nodes.summary: The Electron app's always-on-top window over the desktop: the flame, its pill and the menu-bar item.

nodes.label: Web clipper
nodes.summary: The browser extension that clips a page or a selection into a sphere's recall, talking only to the daemon.

nodes.label: Portal
nodes.summary: The account web service that signs people and their devices in and knows which groups each account belongs to.

nodes.label: Daemon
nodes.summary: The always-on local process where product logic lives.

nodes.label: Door
nodes.summary: The virgil-serve service that answers a request; it never streams.

nodes.label: Worker
nodes.summary: The virgil-serve service that runs the outbox, events and lifecycle work.

nodes.label: Delivery
nodes.summary: The virgil-serve service that sends through providers.

nodes.label: Realtime edge
nodes.summary: The only live transport: it carries signed bundles of committed records to each reader scope.

nodes.label: Postgres
nodes.summary: A cell's database: the committed records, their outbox and the event tables the door and the workers share.

nodes.label: SQLite replica
nodes.summary: A device's local copy of the records it may read, which the daemon answers reads from.

nodes.label: Cloud KMS
nodes.summary: The key service that guards document maintenance: a member's device wraps a document's key to it, the door reads only its public key, and only the worker may decrypt, to compact the document.

nodes.label: Cato
nodes.summary: The merge agent: it readies a draft pull request, verifies it merged onto main and moves main to that commit.

nodes.label: Messo
nodes.summary: The maintenance agent: it works the rulebook sweep's findings and reported bugs into draft pull requests.

nodes.label: Providers
nodes.summary: Slack, Telegram and Discord, which the daemon's comms adapters connect, and the push services delivery sends through.

nodes.label: Blob store
nodes.summary: Cloudflare R2, which holds encrypted attachment bytes, sealed ranges and bot media; the door grants capability URLs to it.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Realtime
nodes.summary: The SFU that carries a huddle's audio and video between participants; the door opens its sessions and mints TURN credentials, and the app sends media to it.

nodes.label: Clerk
nodes.summary: The sign-in service behind the portal's browser pages, where a person signs in to approve a device.

nodes.label: CI
nodes.summary: The GitHub Actions run that tests a change: lanes chosen by the paths it touches, each on its own runner, and ci-gate waiting on every lane it asked for.

nodes.label: Cell deploy
nodes.summary: The workflow that ships the cell when main moves: it builds the virgil-serve image, deploys the edge first, then the door, worker and delivery, and proves each revision is serving.

nodes.label: Production release
nodes.summary: The release number a person bumps and merges by hand to apply production infrastructure; Cato never lands it.

nodes.summary: The Google Cloud project each environment, staging or production, lives in.

nodes.label: Enabled cloud APIs
nodes.summary: The Google Cloud APIs each environment's project turns on.

nodes.label: Private services range
nodes.summary: The address range reserved for Google's side of the private peering Cloud SQL lives behind.

nodes.label: Private network
nodes.summary: The environment's VPC: Cloud SQL has no public address, so reaching it means being inside this network.

nodes.label: Private subnet
nodes.summary: A subnet reserved for the door's compute on the private network; nothing runs in it today.

nodes.label: Private services peering
nodes.summary: The peering that makes Google's Cloud SQL network routable from the private network.

nodes.label: Telemetry writers
nodes.summary: Lets the hosted services write traces and metrics to Cloud's telemetry API; daemons upload through the door instead.

nodes.label: PR environment identity pool
nodes.summary: The GitHub identity federation the PR environment controller signs in through, with no key.

nodes.label: PR environment identity provider
nodes.summary: Accepts this repository's GitHub workflow tokens for the PR environment controller.

nodes.label: PR environment roles
nodes.summary: Lets the PR environment controller read Cloud Run and IAM and add and read PR secrets in the staging project.

nodes.label: PR edge keys
nodes.summary: Each PR slot's edge publishing key.

nodes.label: PR edge key readers
nodes.summary: Lets each PR slot read its edge key.

nodes.label: PR environment account
nodes.summary: The identity the PR environment controller runs as.

nodes.label: PR environment federation
nodes.summary: Lets GitHub workflows act as the PR environment account.

nodes.label: PR environment inventory
nodes.summary: The bucket holding which PR environments should exist and what each one observed.

nodes.label: PR inventory access
nodes.summary: Who may write and read the PR environment inventory.

nodes.label: Fixture identity pool

nodes.summary: Accepts this repository's CI workflow tokens for the fixture bucket.

nodes.label: Fixture provisioner roles

nodes.summary: The APIs the fixture bucket and its federation need.
